subject: SIG: Follow-up - Encryption controls & rotation evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acmefinance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmefinance.com
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: encryption in transit / at rest, KMS usage

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the kickoff call earlier. As we finalize the SIG inventory, a few specific items came up from our controls owners that we couldn't fully resolve from the questionnaire:

1) Encryption in transit: confirm TLS versions supported for both API (hosted) and Private deployments, and whether mTLS is available for Private.
2) Encryption at rest: high-level description of what’s encrypted (models, token logs, snapshots) and whether envelope encryption is used.
3) KMS/HSM: do you use a cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS / GCP KMS) or a dedicated HSM for key material? Any customer-managed key options?
4) Key rotation: describe rotation cadence for root/CMK and data keys, whether rotation is automatic or manual, and what artifacts you can provide (rotation logs, KMS key metadata).

Can you send a short hashed summary we can include in the SIG and let us know what evidence you can hand back (redacted logs, configuration screenshots, attestation)? Our timeline is tight—ideally we’d get a response and evidence by EOD Tuesday so we can close the control owner loop.

Appreciate it—happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

—Jordan
Security Engineer, Acme Finance
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acmefinance.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption in transit / at rest, KMS usage

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a one-page matrix that maps each SIG control question to our statement + available evidence (redwood-sig-encryption-matrix.pdf). Quick summary:

- Encryption in transit: Hosted API uses TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 (TLS 1.3 preferred). Private deployments support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can be configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) at the customer’s network edge; we document mTLS setup in our private deployment runbook.

- Encryption at rest: All customer data (input/output logs, model checkpoints we persist for versioning, and embeddings) are encrypted at rest using AES-256. Keys are envelope-encrypted: data encrypted with per-tenant data keys that are themselves protected by a customer- or Redwood-managed CMK in KMS. Snapshots retained for rollback are also encrypted.

- KMS/HSM: We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For hosted customers by default we use Redwood-managed CMKs in the cloud provider; we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for accounts that require it. For Private (on-premair-gapped) deployments, customers can plug in HSM-backed KMS via our KMS adapter (we certify FIPS-enabled HSMs in the runbook).

- Key rotation: Data keys are rotated on re-encryption cycles (usage-based) — typically short-lived and rotated automatically by the runtime for performance caches. CMKs (customer/master keys) rotation cadence is configurable; by default Redwood-managed CMKs are rotated per provider best practice (every 2 years for CMK metadata rotation) but we also rotate data keys more frequently. For customer-managed keys, rotation is controlled by the customer; we can ingest new key versions without data re-encryption in place by referencing KMS key versioning.

Evidence we can provide this week (attached/links):
- redwood-sig-encryption-matrix.pdf (answer mapping + evidence types)
- rotation-example-log.csv (sample rotation metadata — timestamps and key version changes, redacted tenant ids)
- link to private runbook excerpt (configured mTLS steps)

Neha will follow up with a short attestation note and jonas will coordinate delivering the redacted rotation logs. If you need a specific KMS API response (e.g., keyMetadata from AWS KMS DescribeKey) we can produce a redacted screenshot or exported JSON with identifiers hashed.

Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-sig-encryption-matrix.pdf (application/pdf), rotation-example-log.csv (text/csv)
From: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acmefinance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmefinance.com
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption in transit / at rest, KMS usage

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our infra team:

- For DM-ENCR-4 (key rotation) they want to confirm whether you can provide a time-ordered list of CMK key version creations and the API response for DescribeKey/KeyMetadata for at least one rotation event. Redacted is fine (we just need timestamps and version ids).
- For DM-ENCR-2 (in-transit) we’d like to confirm cipher suites for TLS 1.3 (is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 enabled, etc.) and whether you perform TLS renegotiation.

Can you indicate what format you’ll deliver these in and a target ETA? If possible we’d like the rotation artifacts by EOD Wednesday.

—Jordan
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Willis <jordan.willis@acmefinance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption in transit / at rest, KMS usage

Jordan — thanks, we can provide what you requested. Plan below:

1) Rotation artifacts: we’ll export a time-ordered CSV (rotation-example-log.csv attached) containing key_id (hashed), event_type (CreateKeyVersion/Rotate), timestamp (UTC), and key_version_id (hashed). We will also include a redacted AWS DescribeKey JSON for one rotation event with identifiable strings hashed. Deliverable ETA: Wed 2027-10-06 18:00 UTC.

2) TLS cipher suites: per our TLS baseline, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 are enabled for TLS 1.3; TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 is enabled for TLS 1.2. We do not perform TLS renegotiation; we use session resumption via tickets where applicable. We can provide an exported OpenSSL s_client scan and a config snippet from our load balancer (suitable redactions) — ETA: Wed 2027-10-06 18:00 UTC.

3) Evidence handback: files will be uploaded to a Redacted-share link (Drive link above) and we’ll upload the hashed DescribeKey output to that folder. We will also add a short attestation email signed by our security lead confirming the exports are unaltered.

If that timeline works I’ll proceed; otherwise let me know earlier times and we’ll queue a brief call.

Thanks—Neha
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
